text: parseDuration's case for the 'h' unit multiplies by 60_000 instead of 3_600_000, so hours are computed as minutes; fixing it means changing that one multiplier to 3_600_000.
parseDuration validates input with one regex covering ms|s|m|h|d before doing arithmetic, so a malformed string throws before any unit math runs.

parseDuration's unit handling is a switch over the regex's second capture group, one case per unit constant in milliseconds; adding a new unit means one more case plus updating the regex's alternation.
slugify normalizes with NFKD before stripping accents, so a decomposed diacritic (a base letter followed by a combining mark) is removed by the accent-strip regex rather than left in the output.
slugify lowercases and trims before collapsing non-alphanumeric runs into a single dash, so leading or trailing whitespace never turns into a leading or trailing dash.
slugify's dash-collapse regex is [^a-z0-9]+ replaced by a single '-', run after lowercasing, so runs of punctuation or spaces of any length become exactly one dash.
slugify strips leading and trailing dashes as a separate final regex pass, after the dash-collapse step, so a string that starts or ends with punctuation never leaves a stray dash at either end.
parseDuration's ms case returns the parsed number unchanged, with no multiplier, since milliseconds are already the function's output unit.

describeSchedule (src/schedule.ts, added by the schedule-feature task) composes three existing helpers: slug from slugify, everyMs from parseDuration, and label from titleCase plus formatDuration; a bug in any of the three propagates into describeSchedule's output without a describeSchedule-specific test catching it directly.

titleCase (added for the schedule feature) must exist before describeSchedule's label field can be assembled, since label is titleCase(name) + ' every ' + formatDuration(everyMs); implementing schedule.ts before strings.ts's titleCase lands leaves describeSchedule unable to typecheck.

formatDuration (added for the schedule feature) is the inverse of parseDuration: parseDuration turns a '1h 30m'-shaped string into milliseconds and formatDuration turns milliseconds back into that same space-separated, largest-unit-first text.

tests/duration.test.ts imports parseDuration from '../src/duration.js' (the compiled extension, not .ts) even though the source file is duration.ts, because the fixture's tsconfig uses NodeNext module resolution, which requires the .js extension in relative imports regardless of the source file's real extension.

tests/strings.test.ts's accent-stripping case ('Crème brûlée!' becomes 'creme-brulee') is the one test that actually exercises slugify's NFKD normalize step; a change that breaks accent handling but keeps plain-ASCII slugs passing would slip past every other test in the fixture.

the ts-basic fixture's typecheck command is 'tsc --noEmit' (package.json's typecheck script), separate from its test command 'vitest run'; a task's mustPass list in tasks/ts-basic.json runs both because a change can pass tests while still failing to typecheck.

the lessons table in the memory store is add-only by database trigger, not just convention: lessons_no_delete and lessons_no_rewrite abort in SQLite itself, so a superseded lesson is superseded_by a new row, never edited or deleted in place.

recallLessons fuses BM25 and cosine-over-vectors with reciprocal rank fusion (1/(60+rank) per side) rather than a weighted sum of raw scores, so neither side's score scale has to be normalized against the other before combining.

recallLessons only re-checks a lesson's citation and can mark it stale when checkoutDir is a real project root (it contains a .doug directory); passing a bare temp directory as checkoutDir silently returns checked:false instead of validating anything, which looks like a clean pass rather than a skipped check.

memory.embeddings is null by default in .doug/config.json, so createProvider returns null and every recall runs keyword-only until an operator opts in to an embedding provider; the store never silently starts spending on embedding calls.

Ollama lists a pulled model with a ':tag' suffix (embeddinggemma:latest) even when .doug/config.json names the model bare; doctor's model-present check has to compare on the part before ':' on both sides or it reports a pulled model as missing.

plan.mjs json attaches recalled lessons to a task only when .doug/.state/memory/memory.db already exists on disk, checked before importing lib/memory.mjs at all, so a repository with no memory store never pays node:sqlite's load cost or its ExperimentalWarning.

a task's memoryUsed in the workflow report is [] both when no lesson matched and when the task reused an earlier branch or never launched an implementer at all; reading a [] there as 'memory found nothing relevant' conflates three different situations.

a worker's partial:true claim is only accepted after the harness's own measured context reading at or above the threshold; the SubagentStop gate refuses a self-declared partial with no such reading, so a worker cannot decide on its own that it is out of room.

a partial worker result's handoff carries completed, remaining, next, and verify; remaining and every string in it must be non-empty, so a handoff can never claim there is nothing left while also saying it stopped early.

the stop gate's scope check skips files matched by an ALWAYS_ALLOWED list and an optional ignore list before comparing the rest against the plan's owned files, so a file that looks out of scope in a diff may still be one the gate never judged at all.

harness work under plugins/, packages/doug-codex, and evals/ lands by hand via /core-next, never through the doug-implement workflow on itself; product features go through /doug-next instead, so a bug in the workflow is never the only thing standing between the harness and its own next fix.

a lesson's id is a sha256 of its kind, citation, and text truncated to 16 hex characters, computed once by addLesson; two lessons with the same kind, citation, and text collide on id and addLesson refuses the second insert rather than silently duplicating it.
